summary: Petition under Section 79 (1) (k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 19(3) of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) (First Amendment) Regulations, 2024 seeking extension of infirm power injection and Regulation 57 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 and Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations. A-8A, EOC, NTPC, Sector 24, Noida, Gautam Budh Nagar, Uttar Pradesh-201301 . ** Petitioner** The present Petition has been filed by the NTPC Renewable Energy Limited (hereinafter referred to as “the Petitioner”) seeking extension of injection of infirm power up to 31.1.2026 for the purpose of charging and initiating trial run of the elements, namely, ICR-6 & ICR-12 to 22 in Plot 2 and ICR–9 in Plot 4, forming part of _(c) Grant an extension for injection of infirm power to the Petitioner up to 31.01.2026 for the purpose of charging and initiating trial run of the balance elements i.e., ICR-6 and 12 to 22 (Plot-2) & ICR-9 (Plot-4) out of 1255 MW Capacity being developed at Khavda Solar Park under Phase-II of the CPSU Scheme;_ _(e) Pass such other order(s)/direction(s) which this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in light of the facts and circumstances of the present case and in the interest of justice.”_ (a) The Petitioner, a generating company under Section 2(28) of the Act, and a wholly owned subsidiary of NTPC Green Energy Limited (a subsidiary of NTPC Limited), is a Central Government-owned company falling under the jurisdiction of this Commission under Section 79(1)(a) of the Act. 3. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner mainly reiterated the submissions made in the Petition and, in addition, sought a further extension beyond the stipulated period of 135 days in terms of the proviso to Regulation 19(3) of the IEGC, 2023. Vide the Record of Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as “RoP”) dated 16.10.2025, the Petitioner was directed to clarify (i) the reasons for noncompletion of the trial run and commissioning of the part capacity after obtaining FTC approval for the same, (ii) the reasons for seeking approval for infirm injection up to 31.01.2026, and (iii) to furnish the tentative activity chart with certain other details in the prescribed format. 4. In compliance with the RoP dated 16.10.2025, the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 24.10.2025 has submitted as under: 5. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has complied with the directions issued vide RoP dated 16.10.2025 and, in compliance thereof, has filed an affidavit dated 24.10.2025 furnishing the requisite information sought. The learned counsel further submitted that, as stated in paragraph 10 of the said affidavit, certain blocks in Plot-2 continue to remain waterlogged due to the heavy rainfall experienced in September 2025, which has adversely impacted the testing and commissioning activities. In response to the Commission’s observation that the Petitioner’s request for extension of infirm power injection up to 31.1.2026 under proviso to Regulation 19(3) of the IEGC 2023 appears to be on the higher side, the learned counsel, on instructions, submitted that the Commission may consider granting extension up to 31.12.2025. After hearing the submissions of the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the matter was reserved for order. 8. Even after the above extension by WRLDC, Petitioner completed the trial run and commissioning of 14 elements (plot-2: 5 nos and plot-4: 9 nos), whereas 13 remaining (plot-2: 12 nos and plot-4: 1 nos) elements have not been commissioned. Petitioner is praying to grant an extension to inject infirm power up to 31.12.2025 so that balance elements could be commissioned and condone the delay in filing of the instant Petition. 9. We have perused the submissions of the Petitioner and the information on record. The issues that arise for our consideration are as under: - **2) Whether the Petitioner can be granted an extension of time for the injection of infirm power?** _The Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected person to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of any of these regulations, applicable to a class of persons.”_ As per the above, the extension for injection of infirm power beyond three months from the approval by WRLDC is to be provided by the Commission, and an 11. In the instant case, the WRLDC vide letters dated 30.07.2025 (for FTC ID: 1165) and 16.07.2025 (for FTC ID: 1167) granted extension for injection of infirm power up to 14.09.2025 and 21.09.2025, respectively. Therefore, Petitioner should have filed the instant Petition by 30.08.2025 and 06.09.2025 for FTC ID 1165 and 1167, respectively. However, we observe that the instant Petition was filed on 03.10.2025 with reference no. 600/2025, after a delay of about one month. Petitioner has sought condonation of the delay in filing the instant application under the Commission's Power to Relax. 12. Petitioner has sought permission for infirm power injection for uncommissioned 13 elements i.e. ICR-6 and 12 to 22 **(Plot-2)** & ICR-9 **(Plot-4)** in the following manner: 14. Petitioner has mentioned the following reasons for non-completion of trial and 16. As discussed above, we condone the delay in filing the Petition and allow the Petitioner under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code an extension of the period for interchange of power, latest up to two months from the date of issuance of this Order. Petitioner is directed to complete all commissioning activities related to the project capacity under the instant Petition and achieve COD within the allowed period. **Order in Petition No. 854/MP/2025** CERC Website S.
